report_name: Marquis Software Ransomware Attack Breaches 670,000 Bank Customers

threat_actors.name: Unidentified Ransomware Group
threat_actors.description: The unnamed ransomware group responsible for the supply chain attack on Marquis Software, leading to a data breach affecting customers of U.S. community banks.

attack_patterns.name: Supply Chain Compromise
attack_patterns.description: The attackers compromised Marquis Software, a third-party technology vendor, to gain access to data from its downstream community bank clients.

attack_patterns.name: Data Encrypted for Impact
attack_patterns.description: The attackers deployed ransomware to encrypt systems within Marquis Software's network as part of a double-extortion campaign.

attack_patterns.name: Exfiltration Over C2 Channel
attack_patterns.description: The attackers exfiltrated large volumes of data belonging to banking customers before deploying ransomware, a tactic common in double-extortion campaigns.

attack_patterns.name: Lateral Movement
attack_patterns.description: The attackers likely moved laterally within Marquis Software's network to access systems storing client data for exfiltration.

attack_patterns.name: Inhibit System Recovery
attack_patterns.description: The attackers likely used commands such as vssadmin or wbadmin to delete volume shadow copies or backups to prevent recovery, a common precursor to ransomware deployment.

tools.name: vssadmin
tools.description: Used by attackers to delete volume shadow copies to inhibit system recovery before deploying ransomware.

tools.name: wbadmin
tools.description: Used by attackers to delete backups to inhibit system recovery before deploying ransomware.

identities.name: Marquis Software
identities.description: A U.S.-based technology vendor for community banks that was the direct victim of a ransomware attack, leading to a supply chain breach affecting its clients.

identities.name: U.S. community banks
identities.description: Downstream victims of the Marquis Software supply chain attack, whose data for over 670,000 customers was compromised.

indicators.name: VSSAdmin Shadow Copy Deletion
indicators.pattern:
title: VSSAdmin Shadow Copy Deletion
id: 5a3c1b8e-1d9f-4e8a-9f6b-8c7d6e5f4a3b
status: experimental
description: Detects the use of vssadmin.exe to delete volume shadow copies, a common ransomware precursor technique.
references:
  - https://www.financexmagazine.com/post/a-900-million-deepfake-tab-dora-s-first-real-enforcement-wave-and-a-ransomware-hit-that-should-wo
author: cyber.netsecops.io
date: 2026-11-09
tags:
  - attack.t1490
  - attack.impact
logsource:
  category: process_creation
  product: windows
detection:
  selection:
    Image|endswith: '\vssadmin.exe'
    CommandLine|contains|all:
      - 'delete'
      - 'shadows'
  condition: selection
falsepositives:
  - Legitimate administrative activity, though rare for this specific command combination.
level: high
indicators.description: Detects the use of vssadmin.exe to delete volume shadow copies, a common ransomware precursor technique mentioned as a hunting hint in the report.
